description: Arizona-only rules checked against the cited statutes and official DMV pages. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Approaching a school crossing in Arizona, a speed over which number is prima facie evidence that the speed is unreasonable?
questions.explanation: ARS 28-701(B)(1) says any speed in excess of 15 miles per hour approaching a school crossing is prima facie evidence that the speed is too great and therefore unreasonable, unless a special hazard requires a lesser speed or subsections C or D apply.

questions.q: In an Arizona business or residential district, the prima facie speed in ARS 28-701 is
questions.explanation: ARS 28-701(B)(2) treats any speed over 25 miles per hour in a business or residential district as prima facie evidence that the speed is unreasonable, except as subsections C and D provide or when a special hazard requires a lesser speed.

questions.q: In locations other than a school crossing or a business or residential district, Arizona's prima facie speed is
questions.explanation: ARS 28-701(B)(3) sets 65 miles per hour in other locations as the prima facie unreasonable speed. Section 28-701(C) allows those limits to be altered as authorized in sections 28-702 and 28-703. A state-highway limit set under section 28-702 is effective when appropriate signs are erected.

questions.q: Arizona's criminal excessive-speed statute, ARS 28-701.02, prohibits
options: Exceeding 15 mph approaching a school crossing
Exceeding 35 mph approaching a school crossing
Driving 65 mph where no sign is posted
Driving 5 mph over any posted limit
questions.explanation: ARS 28-701.02(A)(1) prohibits exceeding 35 miles per hour approaching a school crossing. That criminal threshold is separate from the 15 mph prima facie school-crossing speed in section 28-701.

questions.q: If no speed limit is posted in an Arizona business or residential district, ARS 28-701.02 prohibits a speed in excess of
questions.explanation: ARS 28-701.02(A)(2) says a person shall not exceed the posted speed in a business or residential district by more than 20 miles per hour or, if no speed limit is posted, exceed 45 miles per hour.

questions.q: Arizona's DUI per se alcohol concentration, measured within two hours of driving or actual physical control, is
questions.explanation: ARS 28-1381(A)(2) applies when the alcohol concentration is 0.08 or more within two hours and results from alcohol consumed before or while driving or being in actual physical control.

questions.q: For a commercial motor vehicle that requires a commercial driver license, Arizona's alcohol-concentration offense in ARS 28-1381 is
options: Any alcohol only for drivers under 21
questions.explanation: ARS 28-1381(A)(4) uses 0.04 or more for a commercial motor vehicle that requires a commercial driver license. Subsection (A)(5) uses the same 0.04 figure for a vehicle for hire and for a transportation network company driver providing transportation network services.

questions.q: Arizona law makes it unlawful for a person under 21 to drive or be in physical control of a motor vehicle
options: While any alcohol is in the body
questions.explanation: ARS 4-244, paragraph 34, prohibits a person under twenty-one from driving or being in physical control while there is any spirituous liquor in the person's body. That paragraph, as published, does not list an exception.

questions.q: If an Arizona driver accumulates 8 or more points in any 12-month period, ADOT says the result may be
options: Traffic Survival School or a license suspension
Automatic revocation for one year in every case
questions.explanation: ADOT's Points Assessment page says 8 or more points in any 12-month period may require Traffic Survival School or a suspension of the driving privilege for up to 12 months. When one stop produces multiple violations, the highest point value is used.

questions.q: On ADOT's point table, a DUI conviction and a speeding conviction are assessed
questions.explanation: ADOT lists DUI, extreme DUI, reckless driving, and aggressive driving at 8 points, and speeding at 3 points. All other moving violations on that table are 2 points.

questions.q: For the first 6 months, an Arizona class G licensee shall not drive on a public highway from 12:00 a.m. to 5:00 a.m. unless
options: With a licensed parent, or for work
There is no exception until age 21
The only passenger is a sibling
questions.explanation: ARS 28-3174(D) states that midnight-to-5:00 a.m. restriction and those two exceptions for the first six months. Subsection K says the restriction does not apply beginning on the licensee's eighteenth birthday. A parent or legal guardian with a class A, B, C, or D license sits beside the licensee, or the licensee is driving directly to or from a sanctioned school-sponsored activity, work, a sanctioned religious activity, or a family emergency.

questions.q: During the first 6 months, an Arizona class G licensee shall not drive with more than one passenger under 18 unless
options: The vehicle has a back seat
questions.explanation: ARS 28-3174(E) sets that first-six-month passenger limit. It does not apply to the licensee's siblings, and it does not apply when a parent or legal guardian with a class A, B, C, or D license occupies the seat beside the licensee. Subsection K ends the restriction on the licensee's eighteenth birthday.

questions.q: In Arizona, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Arizona issues a learner's permit for a car at 15½ years at the earliest.

questions.q: In Arizona, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Arizona requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

provenance.manual: Permit Test (at Home or in an Office) | Department of Transportation

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Arizona complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Arizona requires 30 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

questions.q: Of a Arizona teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Arizona requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.

provenance.manual: Teen Driver Guide to Class G Permit and License | Department of Transportation

questions.q: In Arizona, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Arizona, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

provenance.manual: 28-3174 - Class G driver licenses; restrictions; civil penalties; motorcycles

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Arizona not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Arizona restricts provisional drivers from Midnight to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Arizona car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Arizona car knowledge test has 30 questions.

provenance.manual: Permit Test (at Home or in an Office) | Department of Transportation

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Arizona car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Arizona car knowledge test.

provenance.manual: Permit Test (at Home or in an Office) | Department of Transportation

questions.q: In Arizona, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Arizona, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.

provenance.manual: 28-1381 - Driving or actual physical control while under the influence

questions.q: In Arizona, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Arizona sets the under-21 limit at 0.00%.

questions.q: In Arizona, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Arizona brings a suspension of 1 year.

provenance.manual: 28-1321 - Implied consent; tests; refusal to submit to test; definition

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Arizona?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Arizona can be posted up to 75 mph for cars.

provenance.manual: 28-702.04 - Maximum speed limit on interstate highways outside urbanized areas and within certain counties; definition

questions.q: Which best describes Arizona's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Only texting is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
questions.explanation: Arizona: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

provenance.manual: 28-914 - Use of portable wireless communication device while driving; prohibition; civil penalty; state preemption; definitions

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Arizona?
options: Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Arizona, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.

questions.q: How is Arizona's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
No seat belt law for adults
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
questions.explanation: Arizona seat belt enforcement is secondary.

provenance.manual: 28-909 - Vehicle restraints required; exceptions; civil penalty

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Arizona?
questions.explanation: Arizona requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.

provenance.manual: 28-907 - Child restraint systems; civil penalty; exemptions; notice; child passenger restraint fund; definitions

questions.q: What is Arizona's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Arizona requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $15,000.

questions.q: Under Arizona's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: Arizona can suspend an adult's license at 8 points in 12 months.
